newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Finding jobs is Arab Gulf states' main challenge.
newsitem.headline: Finding jobs is Arab Gulf states' main challenge.

text.p: The oil-rich Gulf Arab states will face the major challenge of finding more positions for growing job-seekers in the next few years, a Gulf official said.

Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates -- all members in the Gulf Cooperation Council -- are trying to diversify their oil-based economies and to reduce their governments' dominant role.

"The (GCC) biggest future challenge will be finding enough job opportunities to cope with increasing university graduates and job-seekers," head of the Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) Abdul-Rahman al-Jaafari said during a two-day seminar that ended in the Saudi city of Dammam on Wednesday.
The two-day meeting focused on 16 investment projects worth two billion riyals ($5.3 billion).
"The strategic challenge is amending faults in the size of the local labourers' participation in the total workforce which did not exceed 30 percent in 1994," said the GOIC secretary-general.
Jaafari said foreign workers accounted for over 80 percent, and in some cases reached 90 percent, of the labourers working in the GCC's manufacturing industries.
He said GCC governments and their private sectors had to cooperate to provide more jobs.
GCC states have begun a drive to find more jobs for their citizens to reduce reliance on armies of Western expatriates and labourers who help them run their economies.
Jaafari estimated that the GCC population would reach between 56 and 60 million in the next 30 years but he gave no current figures.
